intro_html: Brown stew chicken is the other side of Jamaican cooking, the one that does not involve fire and allspice. You burn a little sugar in the pot until it goes dark, brown the chicken in it, then build a gravy around thyme, scallion, ketchup and bell pepper. Sweet, savory and deeply brown, which is exactly where the name comes from. Over rice, each bowl runs 570 calories and 50 grams of protein for about $1.89.
cost_closing_html: About $1.89 a bowl, and I will be straight with you about where that money goes: chicken thighs are far and away the biggest line on the list. They are also the traditional cut for brown stew chicken, so that money is going exactly where it should.
shop_smart: Chicken thighs are by far the biggest line, so this is the one place to watch the price. Ride the sale cycle on the big club packs, because thighs are already the cheaper and better cut for brown stew. Breast would only cost more and dry out in the gravy.
You do not need bottled browning sauce. It is burnt sugar and water, and this recipe already has brown sugar in it, so caramelizing a spoonful in the pot gets you the same color for free.
Ketchup and worcestershire are the backbone of the gravy and both are pantry items that cost pennies per batch. Store brand ketchup performs identically once it is cooked into a sauce.
Green bell peppers run cheaper than red or yellow almost every week of the year, and green is what this dish traditionally uses, so there is no tradeoff to make.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chicken into large pieces and season it with the black pepper, dried thyme, paprika, salt, grated ginger, minced garlic and half the sliced green onions. Let it sit at least 30 minutes.

Heat the vegetable oil in your largest heavy pot over medium-high, sprinkle in the brown sugar, and let it melt and darken to the color of strong coffee. Do not walk away; the window between browned and burnt is about twenty seconds.
Add the chicken in batches and turn it in the dark sugar until every piece is coated and seared. Set it aside as it browns.
Cook the diced onion and sliced green bell pepper in the same pot for 5 minutes, scraping the bottom to lift the caramel.
Stir in the ketchup, worcestershire sauce and hot sauce, pour in the chicken broth, and bring it to a simmer.

Return the chicken with all its juices, cover, and simmer 30 to 35 minutes until the gravy thickens and the chicken reads 165F. Keep it at a gentle simmer, and the thighs will stay tender and forgiving through the whole cook.
While it simmers, cook the rice and let it steam covered off the heat for 10 minutes, then fold the rice through the stew with the rest of the green onions.
portion_html: Put the pot on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. Same number in every container. Each one lands at 570 calories, and the gravy is what keeps the meat from drying out through a week of microwaving.

steps: Season the cut chicken with thyme, paprika, pepper, ginger, garlic and green onion and rest 30 minutes.
Melt brown sugar in hot oil until dark, then sear the chicken in it in batches.
Soften onion and green bell pepper, then stir in ketchup, worcestershire and hot sauce.
Add broth, return the chicken, cover, and simmer 30 to 35 minutes until the gravy thickens.
Cook the rice, fold it through with the remaining green onions, and portion into 14 containers.
